focused_evidence: The actual generic explicit-RK Definition begins with an open D subset R×R^d and an admitted base pair (t,y)∈D. CTRL1 f is given only on [0,T]×Omega_x×Omega_u. For a fixed cell control, its specialization has no prescribed negative-time values.

If an ambient-open D contained (0,x), some Euclidean ball about that pair would contain negative-time pairs. Thus no such D can both lie within the prescribed CTRL1 domain and admit the initial base time. A stage-time membership test alone cannot establish that supplier hypothesis.

The CTRL1 definition already displays every stage equation and endpoint equation on its actual checked closed-horizon domain. With strictly lower triangular A, the i-th state depends only on previously computed slopes. Induction on the finite stage index evaluates those existing equations or returns the existing first failed query. No ODE existence, open-time extension or new RK method is needed.

At fixed mesh times the decision derivatives are state/control derivatives. The smooth-data/actual-derivative-evaluator hypotheses support such derivatives on their admitted state/control neighborhoods at time 0 or T; no time differentiation or negative-time query is used.
findings.smallest_correction: Use the generic supplier solely for its algebraic coefficient convention; evaluate the already defined CTRL1 equations sequentially for explicit A under the existing closed-horizon query checks. Make those checks expressly cover derivative-evaluator queries.
unsupported_extensions: No defect is asserted in the generic open-domain IVP definition itself. It need not be broadened.
No stage order/stability/convergence promise is added, and no existence or exact solution claim is made for implicit stages.
No unseen extension theorem or external full text is claimed.
